messages.content: Let's continue a release automation project.
Continuing a release automation project.
Anything broken?
A concurrency group cancelling superseded runs came off the board this morning. The logs are easier to read now.
Anything broken?
Once the release settles, splitting the linting job from the test job is where attention goes.
My preference would be test retries limited to two attempts.
Sure, on it. Nobody needs to think about coverage reporting posted to the pull request anymore.
What if we went with semantic versioning driven by commit messages?
OIDC federation instead of long-lived deploy keys is the direction we committed to. Makes sense, doing that.
Anything broken?
CI is passing. The bulk of the diff sits in Makefile. Cutting the pipeline below eight minutes is next up.
Pytest-xdist for test parallelism feels like the right fit here.
Nothing is waiting on anyone at the moment. Broken: cache corruption producing stale build artifacts. Thanks to dependency caching across pipeline runs, the on-call pages stopped. Fine by me.
Where are we?
Complete: quarantining the six flakiest tests. Trunk-based development with short-lived branches is the direction we committed to.
Blockers?
Here's where things stand. Left to do — a rollback job for failed deploys.
I keep coming back to Codecov for coverage tracking.
Fine by me. Automated changelog generation on tag came off the board this morning. The bulk of the diff sits in conftest.py.
Where are we?
The dashboard lit up red with a flaky test failing one run in twenty on the timing assertion. We might revisit this next quarter.
Anything broken?
The dashboard lit up red with test pollution from an unreset global singleton.
